info.title: runic-create
info.description: Guided creator for Runic applications. Run it with dnx Runic.Create.

commands.name: completion
commands.description: Generate bash, zsh, fish or PowerShell completions

options.name: --output
options.description:
Create the project in this directory instead, as dotnet new --output
does.

options.name: --host
options.description:
Window host: desktop opens a native window, cswebui opens a browser
window.

options.name: --linux-gtk
options.description: GTK version of Runic Desktop on Linux: 3 or 4.

options.name: --view-models
options.description: MVVM library for the C# ViewModels.

options.name: --tests
options.description: Add a TUnit test project for the Window. [default: False]

options.name: --nix
options.description:
Add a Nix flake that builds the application with the Runic SDK's
builder. [default: False]

options.name: --packaging
options.description:
Add the packaging/ manifests that dotnet runic package fills, to edit
them: MSIX, macOS bundle, desktop entry, AppStream metadata and
Flatpak manifest. [default: False]

options.name: --restore
options.description:
Restore the project's NuGet packages after creating it, for an IDE
that opens it next. [default: False]

options.name: --force
options.description:
Create the project in a directory that is not empty, as dotnet new
--force does. Files the template writes are replaced.
[default: False]

options.name: --no-install
options.description:
Use the installed Runic.Application.Templates instead of installing
this version, for example offline. [default: False]

options.name: --yes
options.description: Use the default for every option you do not pass instead of asking.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Print the commands without running them. [default: False]

options.name: --template-source
options.description: An additional NuGet source for the template package.

options.name: --application-id
options.description:
The reverse-DNS application ID, such as org.example.Notes: the
desktop entry and Flatpak ID on Linux, the bundle identifier on macOS
and the package name on Windows. Default: com.example. and the
project name's ASCII letters and digits, at most 50 characters, as an
MSIX package name allows.
